headline: A +45% volume surge over four weeks is well-supported by aerobic efficiency, with easy-run HR trending meaningfully lower at comparable effort.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The recent block represents a substantial load increase, but the physiological signal running alongside it is the more important story: your easy-run heart rate has dropped significantly at similar paces, suggesting genuine aerobic adaptation rather than accumulated fatigue. That combination — more volume, better efficiency — is a healthy pattern and justifies continuing to build on the current trajectory.

Today's 18 km easy effort fits cleanly into that picture. At a relaxed pace and moderate HR, it reads as a sound aerobic stimulus without excess cost — appropriate given the step-up in load this block. The 20-week running streak, now at its all-time best, reflects the consistency that underlies these adaptations; it's not a number to chase, but it is evidence of structural training discipline.

The June 27 tempo effort — 15+ km at threshold pace with load well above anything else in the recent window — is the outlier worth holding in mind. That session signals strong top-end aerobic capacity, and the recovery behaviour since (controlled HR, manageable loads) suggests it was absorbed well.
watch_items: Monitor whether easy-run HR continues to decline or begins to plateau — a plateau would be a natural signal to introduce more intensity before further volume
Track how the body handles consecutive load days if back-to-back runs appear in the coming week, given the sustained 4-week build
Strength frequency has ticked up slightly — worth watching whether it's being maintained as run volume rises, since the two qualities are complementary here
Sleep tracking is sparse but consistently short — not a training driver, but worth noting if fatigue accumulates over the next long effort

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 181 km vs 125 km prior block (+45%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 145 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 9 vs 6 runs)
